english.title: Keeper of bovine animal in Wales fail to comply with reasonable requirements to facilitate removal for slaughter
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the keeper of a bovine animal namely **(..SPECIFY ANIMAL..), failed to comply with a reasonable requirement of an inspector or approved veterinary surgeon, with a view to facilitating

(A)_[the identification and examination of that animal by that inspector]_
(B)_[the application to it, or the reading, of any relevant test]_
(C)_[the valuation of it in a case where the Welsh Ministers intend to cause it to be slaughtered under section 32 of the Act in its application to tuberculosis]_
(D)_[the removal of that animal for slaughter]_
english.legislation: Contrary to article 12(2) of the Tuberculosis (Wales) Order 2010 and sections 73 and 75 of the Animal Health Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
keeper of bovine animal / animals
failed to comply with all reasonable requirements of an inspector or approved veterinary surgeon, with a view to facilitating
the identification and examination of that animal by that inspector OR
the application to it, or the reading, of any relevant test OR
the valuation of the animal in a case where the Welsh Ministers intend to cause it to be slaughtered under section 32 of the Act in its application to tuberculosis OR
their removal for slaughter

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: maximum 6 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months
